# Retiring `oldkit`

The application under `app/` is a collection of 18 small demo programs (`app/market`, `app/pantry`, ...). Each one is its own `package main` that formats prices, parses quantities, reads rate tables, groups records, logs events and so on, and prints a few lines. Run one with `go run ./app/NAME`. All modules share the module `shop` (`go.mod`), the record type in `model/`, and two helper packages: the old `oldkit/` and the new `kit/`.

Everything was written against `oldkit`, which is now deprecated. Its replacement, the package `kit`, is complete: **do not edit anything under `kit/`, `model/` or `tests/`**. `oldkit/oldkit.go` itself stays in the repository for now (files cannot be deleted in this job) but nothing may import it any more.

## What has to be true afterwards

1. For every module, `go run ./app/NAME` builds and prints **exactly** what it printed before the migration (byte for byte), exit status 0.
2. The migrated code works when `oldkit` is replaced by a package with the same exported names in which every function panics (that is how the checks run it: any call that still goes to `oldkit` kills the module).
3. The text `oldkit` does not appear in any file under `app/` (imports, comments and strings included), and the files that used it now use `kit` (or `app/common`).

The score is the average of two shares: the share of modules that still build and print the right output with `oldkit` disabled, and the share of files under `app/` that no longer mention `oldkit`.

## The mapping

| `oldkit` | `kit` | what is different |
|---|---|---|
| `FmtAmount(cents int, cur ...string) string` | `kit.Money{Cents: cents, Cur: cur}.Text()` | `Cur` is not optional: the old default was `"EUR"`. |
| `ParseQty(text) (count int, unit string, ok bool)` | `kit.ParseQty(text) (kit.Qty, error)` with `Qty{Count, Unit}` | an `error` replaces the `ok` flag (nil means success). |
| `PadRight(s, width)` | `kit.Pad(s, width, kit.AlignLeft)` | the old name says where the *padding* goes, the alignment says where the *text* goes. |
| `PadLeft(s, width)` | `kit.Pad(s, width, kit.AlignRight)` | same remark. |
| `Title(s)` | `kit.TitleCase(s)` | |
| `CompareNames(a, b) int` | `kit.CompareNames(a, b)` | |
| `Pick(m, keys ...string) any` | `kit.Dig(m, path []string, def any) any` | the keys are one `[]string`; `def` is returned for a missing key (the old function returned `nil`). |
| `Take(xs, n)` | `kit.First(xs, n)` | |
| `GroupBy(items, key) oldkit.Groups` with fields `Keys` (first-seen order) and `M` (key -> items) | `kit.GroupBy(items, key) []kit.Group` with fields `Key` and `Items`, in first-seen order | a slice of buckets replaces the keys-plus-map pair. |
| `Log(level, msg string, kv ...any) string` appends to a global buffer and returns the line | `kit.Default().Emit(level, msg, kit.F{...})` appends to the shared `Events` and returns **nothing**; `kit.Default().Last()` is the most recent line | the key/value pairs become a `kit.F` map. |
| `FlushLog() []string` | `kit.Default().Drain()` | returns the lines and clears them. |
| `Clamp(x, lo, hi)` | `kit.Limit(x, lo, hi)` | |

Functions are also passed around as values (`oldkit.Title` handed to a helper, `[]func(string, int) string{oldkit.PadRight, oldkit.PadLeft}`), and modules import the old package in several styles (`"shop/oldkit"`, `ok "shop/oldkit"`, `. "shop/oldkit"`).

Read `oldkit/oldkit.go` for the exact behaviour of each old function (defaults, formats): the new code must reproduce it. Mind Go's usual rules (an unused import or variable is a compile error).

## How to check your work

* Run every module before you start (`for d in app/*/; do go run ./$d; done > before.txt`) and again at the end: the outputs must be identical.
* `python3 tests/run_examples.py` compares a few modules with the expected output (the real checks cover every module and run with `oldkit` disabled).

# Retiring `oldkit`

The application under `app/` is a collection of 28 small demo programs (`app/glasshouse`, `app/theatre`, ...). Each one is its own `package main` that formats prices, parses quantities, reads rate tables, groups records, logs events and so on, and prints a few lines. Run one with `go run ./app/NAME`. All modules share the module `shop` (`go.mod`), the record type in `model/`, and two helper packages: the old `oldkit/` and the new `kit/`.

Everything was written against `oldkit`, which is now deprecated. Its replacement, the package `kit`, is complete: **do not edit anything under `kit/`, `model/` or `tests/`**. `oldkit/oldkit.go` itself stays in the repository for now (files cannot be deleted in this job) but nothing may import it any more.

## What has to be true afterwards

1. For every module, `go run ./app/NAME` builds and prints **exactly** what it printed before the migration (byte for byte), exit status 0.
2. The migrated code works when `oldkit` is replaced by a package with the same exported names in which every function panics (that is how the checks run it: any call that still goes to `oldkit` kills the module).
3. The text `oldkit` does not appear in any file under `app/` (imports, comments and strings included), and the files that used it now use `kit` (or `app/common`).

The score is the average of two shares: the share of modules that still build and print the right output with `oldkit` disabled, and the share of files under `app/` that no longer mention `oldkit`.

## The mapping

| `oldkit` | `kit` | what is different |
|---|---|---|
| `FmtAmount(cents int, cur ...string) string` | `kit.Money{Cents: cents, Cur: cur}.Text()` | `Cur` is not optional: the old default was `"EUR"`. |
| `ParseQty(text) (count int, unit string, ok bool)` | `kit.ParseQty(text) (kit.Qty, error)` with `Qty{Count, Unit}` | an `error` replaces the `ok` flag (nil means success). |
| `PadRight(s, width)` | `kit.Pad(s, width, kit.AlignLeft)` | the old name says where the *padding* goes, the alignment says where the *text* goes. |
| `PadLeft(s, width)` | `kit.Pad(s, width, kit.AlignRight)` | same remark. |
| `Title(s)` | `kit.TitleCase(s)` | |
| `CompareNames(a, b) int` | `kit.CompareNames(a, b)` | |
| `Pick(m, keys ...string) any` | `kit.Dig(m, path []string, def any) any` | the keys are one `[]string`; `def` is returned for a missing key (the old function returned `nil`). |
| `Take(xs, n)` | `kit.First(xs, n)` | |
| `GroupBy(items, key) oldkit.Groups` with fields `Keys` (first-seen order) and `M` (key -> items) | `kit.GroupBy(items, key) []kit.Group` with fields `Key` and `Items`, in first-seen order | a slice of buckets replaces the keys-plus-map pair. |
| `Log(level, msg string, kv ...any) string` appends to a global buffer and returns the line | `kit.Default().Emit(level, msg, kit.F{...})` appends to the shared `Events` and returns **nothing**; `kit.Default().Last()` is the most recent line | the key/value pairs become a `kit.F` map. |
| `FlushLog() []string` | `kit.Default().Drain()` | returns the lines and clears them. |
| `Clamp(x, lo, hi)` | `kit.Limit(x, lo, hi)` | |

Functions are also passed around as values (`oldkit.Title` handed to a helper, `[]func(string, int) string{oldkit.PadRight, oldkit.PadLeft}`), and modules import the old package in several styles (`"shop/oldkit"`, `ok "shop/oldkit"`, `. "shop/oldkit"`). Part of the application goes through `app/common`, a package of thin wrappers around `oldkit`; the modules that import it need no change if you rewrite `common` (keeping its exported names and signatures) on top of `kit`, or you may migrate those modules directly.

Read `oldkit/oldkit.go` for the exact behaviour of each old function (defaults, formats): the new code must reproduce it. Mind Go's usual rules (an unused import or variable is a compile error).

## How to check your work

* Run every module before you start (`for d in app/*/; do go run ./$d; done > before.txt`) and again at the end: the outputs must be identical.
* `python3 tests/run_examples.py` compares a few modules with the expected output (the real checks cover every module and run with `oldkit` disabled).

# Retiring `oldkit`

The application under `app/` is a collection of 32 small demo programs (`app/chandlery`, `app/glasshouse`, ...). Each one is its own `package main` that formats prices, parses quantities, reads rate tables, groups records, logs events and so on, and prints a few lines. Run one with `go run ./app/NAME`. All modules share the module `shop` (`go.mod`), the record type in `model/`, and two helper packages: the old `oldkit/` and the new `kit/`.

Everything was written against `oldkit`, which is now deprecated. Its replacement, the package `kit`, is complete: **do not edit anything under `kit/`, `model/` or `tests/`**. `oldkit/oldkit.go` itself stays in the repository for now (files cannot be deleted in this job) but nothing may import it any more.

## What has to be true afterwards

1. For every module, `go run ./app/NAME` builds and prints **exactly** what it printed before the migration (byte for byte), exit status 0.
2. The migrated code works when `oldkit` is replaced by a package with the same exported names in which every function panics (that is how the checks run it: any call that still goes to `oldkit` kills the module).
3. The text `oldkit` does not appear in any file under `app/` (imports, comments and strings included), and the files that used it now use `kit` (or `app/common`).

The score is the average of two shares: the share of modules that still build and print the right output with `oldkit` disabled, and the share of files under `app/` that no longer mention `oldkit`.

## The mapping

| `oldkit` | `kit` | what is different |
|---|---|---|
| `FmtAmount(cents int, cur ...string) string` | `kit.Money{Cents: cents, Cur: cur}.Text()` | `Cur` is not optional: the old default was `"USD"`. |
| `ParseQty(text) (count int, unit string, ok bool)` | `kit.ParseQty(text) (kit.Qty, error)` with `Qty{Count, Unit}` | an `error` replaces the `ok` flag (nil means success). |
| `PadRight(s, width)` | `kit.Pad(s, width, kit.AlignLeft)` | the old name says where the *padding* goes, the alignment says where the *text* goes. |
| `PadLeft(s, width)` | `kit.Pad(s, width, kit.AlignRight)` | same remark. |
| `Title(s)` | `kit.TitleCase(s)` | |
| `CompareNames(a, b) int` | `kit.CompareNames(a, b)` | |
| `Pick(m, keys ...string) any` | `kit.Dig(m, path []string, def any) any` | the keys are one `[]string`; `def` is returned for a missing key (the old function returned `nil`). |
| `Take(xs, n)` | `kit.First(xs, n)` | |
| `GroupBy(items, key) oldkit.Groups` with fields `Keys` (first-seen order) and `M` (key -> items) | `kit.GroupBy(items, key) []kit.Group` with fields `Key` and `Items`, in first-seen order | a slice of buckets replaces the keys-plus-map pair. |
| `Log(level, msg string, kv ...any) string` appends to a global buffer and returns the line | `kit.Default().Emit(level, msg, kit.F{...})` appends to the shared `Events` and returns **nothing**; `kit.Default().Last()` is the most recent line | the key/value pairs become a `kit.F` map. |
| `FlushLog() []string` | `kit.Default().Drain()` | returns the lines and clears them. |
| `Clamp(x, lo, hi)` | `kit.Limit(x, lo, hi)` | |

Functions are also passed around as values (`oldkit.Title` handed to a helper, `[]func(string, int) string{oldkit.PadRight, oldkit.PadLeft}`), and modules import the old package in several styles (`"shop/oldkit"`, `ok "shop/oldkit"`, `. "shop/oldkit"`).

Read `oldkit/oldkit.go` for the exact behaviour of each old function (defaults, formats): the new code must reproduce it. Mind Go's usual rules (an unused import or variable is a compile error).

## How to check your work

* Run every module before you start (`for d in app/*/; do go run ./$d; done > before.txt`) and again at the end: the outputs must be identical.
* `python3 tests/run_examples.py` compares a few modules with the expected output (the real checks cover every module and run with `oldkit` disabled).

# Retiring `oldkit`

The application under `app/` is a collection of 36 small demo programs (`app/kiln`, `app/quarry`, ...). Each one is its own `package main` that formats prices, parses quantities, reads rate tables, groups records, logs events and so on, and prints a few lines. Run one with `go run ./app/NAME`. All modules share the module `shop` (`go.mod`), the record type in `model/`, and two helper packages: the old `oldkit/` and the new `kit/`.

Everything was written against `oldkit`, which is now deprecated. Its replacement, the package `kit`, is complete: **do not edit anything under `kit/`, `model/` or `tests/`**. `oldkit/oldkit.go` itself stays in the repository for now (files cannot be deleted in this job) but nothing may import it any more.

## What has to be true afterwards

1. For every module, `go run ./app/NAME` builds and prints **exactly** what it printed before the migration (byte for byte), exit status 0.
2. The migrated code works when `oldkit` is replaced by a package with the same exported names in which every function panics (that is how the checks run it: any call that still goes to `oldkit` kills the module).
3. The text `oldkit` does not appear in any file under `app/` (imports, comments and strings included), and the files that used it now use `kit` (or `app/common`).

The score is the average of two shares: the share of modules that still build and print the right output with `oldkit` disabled, and the share of files under `app/` that no longer mention `oldkit`.

## The mapping

| `oldkit` | `kit` | what is different |
|---|---|---|
| `FmtAmount(cents int, cur ...string) string` | `kit.Money{Cents: cents, Cur: cur}.Text()` | `Cur` is not optional: the old default was `"CHF"`. |
| `ParseQty(text) (count int, unit string, ok bool)` | `kit.ParseQty(text) (kit.Qty, error)` with `Qty{Count, Unit}` | an `error` replaces the `ok` flag (nil means success). |
| `PadRight(s, width)` | `kit.Pad(s, width, kit.AlignLeft)` | the old name says where the *padding* goes, the alignment says where the *text* goes. |
| `PadLeft(s, width)` | `kit.Pad(s, width, kit.AlignRight)` | same remark. |
| `Title(s)` | `kit.TitleCase(s)` | |
| `CompareNames(a, b) int` | `kit.CompareNames(a, b)` | |
| `Pick(m, keys ...string) any` | `kit.Dig(m, path []string, def any) any` | the keys are one `[]string`; `def` is returned for a missing key (the old function returned `nil`). |
| `Take(xs, n)` | `kit.First(xs, n)` | |
| `GroupBy(items, key) oldkit.Groups` with fields `Keys` (first-seen order) and `M` (key -> items) | `kit.GroupBy(items, key) []kit.Group` with fields `Key` and `Items`, in first-seen order | a slice of buckets replaces the keys-plus-map pair. |
| `Log(level, msg string, kv ...any) string` appends to a global buffer and returns the line | `kit.Default().Emit(level, msg, kit.F{...})` appends to the shared `Events` and returns **nothing**; `kit.Default().Last()` is the most recent line | the key/value pairs become a `kit.F` map. |
| `FlushLog() []string` | `kit.Default().Drain()` | returns the lines and clears them. |
| `Clamp(x, lo, hi)` | `kit.Limit(x, lo, hi)` | |

Functions are also passed around as values (`oldkit.Title` handed to a helper, `[]func(string, int) string{oldkit.PadRight, oldkit.PadLeft}`), and modules import the old package in several styles (`"shop/oldkit"`, `ok "shop/oldkit"`, `. "shop/oldkit"`). Part of the application goes through `app/common`, a package of thin wrappers around `oldkit`; the modules that import it need no change if you rewrite `common` (keeping its exported names and signatures) on top of `kit`, or you may migrate those modules directly.

Read `oldkit/oldkit.go` for the exact behaviour of each old function (defaults, formats): the new code must reproduce it. Mind Go's usual rules (an unused import or variable is a compile error).

## How to check your work

* Run every module before you start (`for d in app/*/; do go run ./$d; done > before.txt`) and again at the end: the outputs must be identical.
* `python3 tests/run_examples.py` compares a few modules with the expected output (the real checks cover every module and run with `oldkit` disabled).
